expectations.text: Treats already-published terms with a live affiliate base as pricing each tightening at one amendment cycle plus the affiliates who leave, making reversibility rather than drafting hours the binding constraint.
expectations.evidence: Partial. The answer does treat the amendment cycle as a real cost: it establishes a 15-day notice track for ~300 EU/UK affiliates, bundles both new clauses (brand bidding + fake reviews) into a single notice, versions the document ('supersedes v[X-1]') and notes 'you're 14 months into a maintained program, not issuing a one-off.' It also routes around the cycle's latency for the urgent case — 'don't wait for the amendment cycle to deal with them... existing language plus ordinary trademark law likely already gives you grounds to suspend... today.' Attrition appears only as a legal requirement

expectations.text: Treats already-published terms with a live affiliate base as pricing each tightening at one amendment cycle plus the affiliates who leave, making reversibility rather than drafting hours the binding constraint.
expectations.evidence: The answer surfaces the two raw ingredients of the cost but never prices them or draws the conclusion. It notes the 15-day notice window and that 'An affiliate who does not accept an amendment may terminate their participation in the Program at no cost' — but purely as a P2B legal requirement, not as a business cost attached to every future tightening. There is no advice to bundle anticipated future changes into this single amendment cycle, no mention of churn risk across the 1,100-affiliate base as a reason to get the scope right now, and no framing of reversibility as the binding constraint.
